clue.text: Anorexic over losing money?

parts.note: pounds here are units of body weight rather than sterling, so someone who sheds them is in financial trouble only on the surface

explanation.surface: A question about someone with an eating disorder fretting over a financial loss.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'losing money' as an anorexic person losing pounds of weight: the phrase for being financially poorer then describes them literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means financially poorer, and losing pounds of weight is exactly what an anorexic does.

clue.text: How gate-crashers gain entry to the party

definitions.text: How gate-crashers gain entry to the party

parts.words: How gate-crashers gain entry to the party
parts.note: describes intruders who arrive at a party without an invitation

explanation.surface: A description of how uninvited guests get into a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Gate-crashers turn up without being invited, so they come in uninvited.

clue.text: Backyard transport

indicators.note: back tells us to read the following letters backwards

parts.note: yard is the second half of the clue word Backyard, split from Back, which signals the reversal; the reversed run inside Backyard is a coincidence of that split, not a hidden word

explanation.surface: Something in the garden used to move goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backyard' looks like one word, but 'Back' says to read 'yard' backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A dray is a low cart for heavy loads, traditionally brewers' barrels.

clue.text: Finish a package tour of Little Italy

indicators.note: a tour goes round, so the package phrase goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: to package goods is to wrap them up
IT is a short form, 'little' version, of Italy

explanation.surface: Bring to an end a holiday package around the New York district Little Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little Italy' looks like the New York neighbourhood, but 'Little' says to abbreviate Italy to IT, which goes inside WRAP UP.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an informal way of saying to bring something to a close.

clue.text: Burlington House present for the founder of Bart's Hospital

parts.note: the Royal Academy (RA) is housed in Burlington House in Piccadilly
present means here, in attendance

explanation.surface: A gift from a London building for the man who founded a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: Burlington House in London is home to the Royal Academy, RA; 'present' reads as a gift but means HERE. Bart's is St Bartholomew's Hospital in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Rahere was a twelfth-century courtier and monk who established St Bartholomew's Hospital in 1123.

clue.text: Oil — producing plant leaves little bears food

definitions.text: Oil — producing plant leaves little bears food

parts.words: Oil — producing plant leaves little bears food
parts.note: describes a plant whose leaves yield a medicinal oil and feed koalas, the small animals often called bears

explanation.surface: A garden plant that produces oil and whose leaves feed small bears.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'little bears' are koalas, often wrongly called koala bears, which eat only these leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: This Australian gum yields an aromatic oil from its foliage, which is also the koala's diet.

clue.text: Gave signs of being below standard

definitions.meaning: signalled, as with a waved banner

explanation.definitionFit: Flagged means signalled with a banner, and also wilted or tired.

clue.text: Do it in time by changing Henry's coins

indicators.note: changing coins sounds like exchanging money, but here it means the letters change order

parts.note: the possessive S is kept as a letter here

explanation.surface: Henry changes his money in good time.
explanation.definitionFit: To act together in unison is to keep exactly simultaneous timing.

clue.text: Sailor's after Californian wood that can be smoked

indicators.note: the sailor comes after the Californian piece, so it is written second

parts.note: CAL is a short form of California
AB, able seaman, is a sailor; the 's is 'has', joining the clue
ash is a tree and its timber

explanation.surface: A sailor fancies some Californian timber that can be smoked.
explanation.walkthrough: A calabash is a gourd hollowed out to make a tobacco pipe, so it is something smoked.
explanation.definitionFit: The gourd is famously made into tobacco pipes, so it is an item a smoker lights.

clue.text: Careful, it looks fishy

definitions.meaning: char is a fish, so char-y would mean resembling a char

explanation.definitionFit: Chary means cautious; read as char plus -y it means like the fish called char.

clue.text: They're put out about our posters and take legal action

definitions.note: the definition, with They're at the start, describes people who bring cases to court

indicators.note: put out means disturbed, so the following letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: C, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: People upset at our posters go to court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They're' at the start makes the definition people: those who take legal action. 'put out' shuffles C (circa, about) with OUR POSTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: These lawyers bring criminal cases against the accused in court.

clue.text: An inclination to scrape along

definitions.meaning: a slope, as of a theatre stage
to drag a toothed tool over a surface, gathering leaves

explanation.definitionFit: A stage has a slope called its rake, and gardeners draw a toothed tool across lawns to gather leaves.

clue.text: Very little reasoning in dis cussing trivialities

parts.note: micro- is a prefix for very small
logic is the science of reasoning

explanation.surface: Someone talking about petty matters shows hardly any sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names hair-splitting argument over minor details, petty reasoning.

clue.text: Revealed David's 25 roughly

indicators.note: roughly means imprecisely arranged, so the letters are reshuffled

parts.note: the possessive S is kept as a letter here
the number points to the answer of 25-down, the second word of 6-down's phrase

explanation.surface: David's twenty-five is disclosed approximately.
explanation.walkthrough: '25' refers to the answer at 25-down; that word joins DAVIDS in the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something publicly known through notices is to publicise it.

clue.text: Took part with spirit on an instrument

parts.note: sided means took one party's part in a dispute
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: Someone joined a faction while drinking spirits on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a small double-headed drum with snares, a percussion instrument in bands and orchestras.

clue.text: One of our finest leg-spinners

parts.note: reads as praise for a cricket bowler, but means a creature that spins silk with its legs, and very fine silk at that

explanation.surface: Praise for a top cricket bowler who spins the ball from leg.
explanation.walkthrough: A leg-spinner is a type of bowler in cricket; here it is a creature that spins thread using its legs, and 'finest' describes the thread.
explanation.definitionFit: This eight-legged creature produces gossamer, among the finest threads in nature.

clue.text: Accept advice as waiters do

definitions.meaning: receive a gratuity from a customer

explanation.definitionFit: Waiters receive gratuities, and someone heeding a suggestion acts on a pointer.

clue.text: Fencing position right for a past President

parts.note: carte (quarte) is the fourth parry position in fencing

explanation.surface: A fencer takes up a stance suitable for a former head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: Jimmy Carter was the 39th President of the United States.

clue.text: Free from a spell of duty jo

definitions.text: Free from a spell of duty

parts.words: Free from a spell of duty
parts.note: describes taking over from a sentry or worker so that they can stand down

explanation.surface: A guard is let off a shift.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking over someone's watch or shift is the act of standing them down.

clue.text: Cracked china cup replaced by one in good order

indicators.note: a cracked item is broken up, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A broken piece of crockery is swapped for one in perfect condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in good order' reads as undamaged, but it means a member of a religious order; 'replaced by' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: A Capuchin is a friar of a Franciscan religious order.

clue.text: Man embracing girl is a ne Greek

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so the girl's name goes within

parts.note: he stands for a man
Ellen is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A man hugging a girl turns out to be from Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: Hellene is the ancient and formal name for a person from Greece.

clue.text: Study of an abstainer poet? 131

indicators.note: of here means belonging to, so the study comes after the abstainer it belongs to

parts.note: dry describes someone who abstains from alcohol
a den is a private study room

explanation.surface: A question whether a teetotaller's study belongs to a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: John Dryden was the leading English poet of the late seventeenth century, Poet Laureate.

clue.text: Discuss business with Otto!

parts.note: Otto suggests the Ottoman, so chatting with him is speaking to a Turk

explanation.surface: An instruction to hold a business meeting with a man named Otto.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom means to talk frankly about business; Otto stands for the Ottoman, so talking to him is talking Turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to speak frankly and get down to practical dealing.

clue.text: Donations to a pre-nationalised railway system

parts.note: LMS was the London, Midland and Scottish Railway, one of the British companies merged into British Railways in 1948

explanation.surface: Gifts made to one of Britain's old private railway companies.
explanation.walkthrough: The LMS (London, Midland and Scottish) was a British railway company before nationalisation in 1948.
explanation.definitionFit: Alms are charitable gifts of money or food to the poor.

clue.text: See 6
Hears about grounded birds

indicators.note: about can mean around or rearranged, so the letters of the word are turned about

explanation.surface: Someone picks up news about flightless birds.
explanation.definitionFit: These large South American birds cannot fly, so they stay on the ground.

clue.text: Dissuaded to prevent the German's return

parts.note: to deter is to prevent or discourage

indicators.note: return means the German word is read backwards

parts.note: der is the German masculine word for the

explanation.surface: Someone was talked out of stopping a German man coming home.
explanation.definitionFit: Being put off doing something is to be discouraged from it.

clue.text: Recipients haven't a single reason for getting it

definitions.text: Recipients haven't a single reason for getting it

parts.words: Recipients haven't a single reason for getting it
parts.note: seems to say the receivers do not deserve a gift, but means they are no longer single, which is why they receive it

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that the people receiving a gift have done nothing to earn it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'haven't a single reason' sounds like 'no reason at all', but means the couple are no longer single, which is the reason for the gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Couples receive such gifts precisely because they have married and stopped being single.
